summary: The center of the native editor is a persistent canvas/document surface. Everything else is a dockable, floating, or contextual tool panel.
corePrinciples: The canvas/document surface is permanent and never traps access to top-level chrome.
Tools are panels, palettes, inspectors, timelines, browsers, or floating documents; tools are not mutually exclusive full-screen modes by default.
Game/room/world/scene editing happens in the center canvas; supporting workflows attach around it.
Specialized editors remain available, but are expressed as tool panels and document types rather than isolated tab prisons.
Project-specific terms are supplied by the active ProjectProfile, not hardcoded by the editor shell.

responsibilities: draw and edit rooms/scenes/maps/UI/prefabs/patterns/atlases/character documents as active documents
accept tools from dock panels through shared commands

mustNotDo: do not add new whole-editor workspaces for asset intake
do not let a tool panel consume top-level workspace tabs
do not require users to leave the canvas to inspect assets, animation, character, logic, or sound data
